facts.raw_span: severe bilateral pneumonia
recent close contact with a fatal case
No relevant medical history was reported
blurred vision and redness in her right eye
temporary (8-day) pain when mobilizing the globe
Best-corrected visual acuity was +2 logMAR (hand movement) OD
Relative afferent pupil defect
Central scotoma
Positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2
Negative CSF SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR
Cranial MRI with fine optic nerve cuts (normal results)
Fluorescein Angiography (Day 30): Mild leakage associated with inferior peripapillary hemorrhage

concepts.why: The patient tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 via nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR.
The patient developed blurred vision, redness, and pain in the right eye, with relative afferent pupil defect and central scotoma, after testing positive for SARS-CoV-2.
The patient was hospitalized for severe bilateral pneumonia and tested positive for SARS-CoV-2.
The patient developed optic neuritis after being hospitalized for pneumonia, which may be related to a post-infectious complication.
The patient had fluorescein angiography showing mild leakage associated with inferior peripapillary hemorrhage, which may be related to SARS-CoV-2 infection.
The patient was hospitalized for severe bilateral pneumonia and tested positive for SARS-CoV-2, indicating a viral etiology.
The patient had a relative afferent pupil defect and central scotoma, with fluorescein angiography showing mild leakage associated with inferior peripapillary hemorrhage.
The patient had fluorescein angiography showing mild leakage associated with inferior peripapillary hemorrhage, which may be related to a viral etiology.
It explains the central scotoma and normal cranial MRI results with fine optic nerve cuts.

rationales.F04: Blurred vision and redness in one eye are symptoms of optic neuritis and retinal vasculitis.
rationales.F06: Best-corrected visual acuity of +2 logMAR indicates severe visual impairment, consistent with optic neuritis.
rationales.F07: Relative afferent pupil defect is a sign of optic neuritis.
rationales.F08: Central scotoma is a symptom of optic neuritis.
rationales.F09: Positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2 indicates COVID-19 infection.
rationales.F12: Fluorescein Angiography showing mild leakage associated with inferior peripapillary hemorrhage is consistent with optic neuritis and retinal vasculitis.
